scope: INT-KEY-001, INT-KEY-002, INT-SEC-001 — user-selected subset of the audit above
New API: /api/applications/members (list, invite, remove, manage roles) — kapp_-key-authenticated, scoped to the calling application's own organization
incidentalFindingClosed: POST /api/invitations/accept granted an invitation's role_id via a service_role client with no owner-role check — any org Admin could create an owner-role invitation and have it silently grant real Owner on acceptance, bypassing every owner-grant protection built in migrations 0025-0031. Closed via migration 0033: invitations can never reference the Owner role, for any caller.

scope: Application registration/ownership lifecycle — scoped re-audit, not full-app
note: Two sides of one root cause: no self-service application creation/ownership-claim flow exists anywhere (CLI-only, no org context at registration time), and owner_organization_id is never written by any code path — confirmed by exhaustive grep. INT-KEY-001's rotate/revoke UI and the new /api/applications/members API are both correctly built but practically unreachable in a fresh deployment as a result.

scope: INT-API-007, INT-API-008 — user approved the recommended fix shape from the prior scoped AUDIT
incidentalFindingClosed: CRITICAL, not tracked as an integration-surface gap (recorded as PQ-SEC-010 in kontrolia-professional-review's issues.json instead, since it's a pre-existing regression unrelated to this feature's own design): migration 0030 silently dropped the is_platform_admin JWT claim, found live while testing this route with a real platform-admin session. Fixed via migration 0035.
note: Also closed an adjacent gap found while designing the claim route: migration 0022's UPDATE policy let a dual-org admin silently reassign an already-owned application to their other org (same shape as PQ-SEC-005). Migration 0034's prevent_application_ownership_reassignment trigger blocks any non-service_role change to owner_organization_id once set.
